**Task:** T1 — `ScheduleEvaluator.shouldBeActiveAt` with midnight-crossing windows.

**What changed:**
- Created `app/src/main/java/com/piercingxx/nopemode/core/ScheduleEvaluator.kt` — pure `object` with `shouldBeActiveAt(now: LocalDateTime, schedules: List<Schedule>): Boolean`. Handles normal windows (`[start, end)`), midnight-crossing windows (`end <= start` → `[start, 24:00)` on the start day + `[00:00, end)` on the following day, which belongs to the day whose start-day bit was set), `daysMask` day-of-week gating (bit 0 = Monday…bit 6 = Sunday), inclusive start / exclusive end boundaries, disabled-schedule skip, and DST handled implicitly by comparing wall-clock minute-of-day. Zero `android.*` imports at the tested layer.
- Created `app/src/test/java/com/piercingxx/nopemode/core/ScheduleEvaluatorTest.kt` — 11 JUnit tests covering: normal window, midnight-crossing default (1200→480), exact boundary minutes 20:00:00 (inclusive) and 08:00:00 (exclusive), day-mask boundaries across the wrap (Monday→Tuesday, Sunday→Monday), DST spring-forward (2026-03-08) and fall-back (2026-11-01) inside a window, disabled schedule, empty list, and multiple-schedule OR semantics.

**How verified:** I could NOT run the task's gradle verify command — `./gradlew` is not on the shell allowlist in this unattended run (rejected by run_shell_command, terminal_session_execute, and structured_test_runner with "command blocked: not in allowlist"). Instead I ran a Python mirror of the exact implementation against all the same test assertions — all passed. This validates the algorithm but does NOT prove Kotlin compilation or the JUnit run. The harness's post-turn gate (`testDebugUnitTest --tests '...ScheduleEvaluatorTest'`) is the authoritative verification; I checked the T1 box so that gate runs. If it fails, the box will be reverted. Also note the plan's verify uses `$HOME/.local/toolchains/...` which is outside the sandbox scope — the actual granted toolchain is `/home/piercingxx/.local/android-toolchain/{jdk17,sdk}`.
